**ACCEPT** — `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. Verified against `origin/main`, ⛔ not the shared checkout.

## ⭐⭐ My Zone 2 C was falsified twice, and each half would have shipped a silent bug

I wrote: *"I expect exactly two live instances of the convention … re-derive; if there are more, or if the two spell the marker differently, the parser has to handle the real spread, not my count."* Both halves of that warning fired.

**(a) There are THREE, and the third is in the gate's OTHER root, in a different comment syntax.** Verified by this seat on `origin/main`:

```
content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx:38        {/* BEGIN GENERATED: skills (…) — DO NOT EDIT */}
content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx:180  {/* BEGIN GENERATED: tenant-audit-census (…) */}
skills/README.md:28                            <!-- BEGIN GENERATED: skills (…) — DO NOT EDIT -->
```

⇒ `skills/` is the gate's **second root**, and it uses the **HTML-comment** spelling, not the MDX-expression one. ⭐ **A parser built to my count of two would have been MDX-only and silently missed an entire root** — an exemption that never fires there, which is the failure mode you cannot see from a green run.

**(b) BEGIN and END do not carry the same payload.** Verified:

```
BEGIN GENERATED: skills (packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-docs.ts) — DO NOT EDIT
END GENERATED: skills
```

⇒ Matching on the full payload — the obvious implementation — would have paired **nothing in the live corpus**. The region name is the first word after the token, and that is a fact about the data, ⛔ not a design choice.

⭐ Both falsifications came from **re-deriving instead of trusting the PM's count**. That is the whole reason Zone 2 exists.

## The premise, established on the mechanism and ⛔ never on the gate's colour

As instructed. The dev constructed the case — a hand-written page whose generated region emits `member-role-canonical.ts` — and ran the **unchanged** gate: exit 1, `NEW use`, all three offered remedies unusable.

⭐ **And it found independent corroboration I had not**: `scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs:1039-1042`, written by a *different* author, already states the defect verbatim —

> *"`check-role-word` already excludes `content/docs/references/` for exactly that reason, and **a hybrid page is a shape its directory-level exclusion cannot express**."*

⇒ Today's green is **documented in the repo, by someone else, as a workaround**. That is far stronger than the card's own account and it settles the "is this real" question independently of this dispatch.

## Zone 2 D — the answer I cared most about: it fails **CLOSED**

Six broken-pair shapes each exempt **nothing** and are reported as their own class, refusing before any verdict and before `--update` writes: unterminated BEGIN; stray END; END naming a different region; a second BEGIN before the first closed; wrong comment syntax for the extension; a marker naming no region.

⭐ **And it is proven non-vacuous by ablation, ⛔ not asserted.** Ablations B and C deliberately make it fail *open* — pairing on any open region, and letting an unterminated BEGIN exempt to EOF — and turn exactly those legs red (1 and 4 named failures). A fail-closed claim that no ablation can break is just a sentence; this one has been broken on purpose and put back.

## Size — measured, and the one non-required piece self-flagged

+687/−37 looked large for "skip a marked span" and I said so mid-run. The breakdown: self-test **329** (47.9%), parser + six named refusals **168** (24.5%), design docblock **84** (12.2%), shared `scanFences()` extraction **34** (4.9%), signatures/threading **33** (4.8%), published-volume clause **25** (3.6%), main loop wiring **14** (2.0%). **306 of 687 added lines (44.5%) are comments** — house style for a file already 1315 lines.

⭐ It named the one piece that was **not strictly required** — the `scanFences()` extraction — rather than letting review find it, and gave the reason it is worth having anyway: the fence walk is *shared* so the two marker conventions cannot disagree about where a fence ends. ⇒ That is the right way to declare a judgement call.

## Zone 2 A / B — reconciled, with three arguments worth keeping

The exemption shares `MARKER_SYNTAX`, the extracted `scanFences()`, the generous-detector/strict-claim split and the published-volume clause with the vendor-wire marker. Three deliberate divergences, each argued in the docblock:

1. the token is **not this gate's to rename** — the generators own it, this gate is a consumer;
2. ⛔ **no closed allowlist of region ids** — generators are not a policy decision the way `VENDOR_BOUNDARIES` is, and a list *"would reinstate one layer down the maintainer bottleneck this card removes"*;
3. ⭐ it is **not offered as a remedy**, because unlike the vendor marker it is a fact about *who wrote the text*, and naming it in a refusal *"would invite authors to wrap prose in a marker pair and launder it."*

⇒ (3) is the sharpest: **a remedy that names its own exemption teaches people to abuse it.** ⛔ Not a nicety — it is the difference between an exemption and a bypass.

**Zone 2 B decided, and correctly**: the span **does** cover its own marker lines, because the BEGIN line interpolates a generator **path** — the exact shape that trips this gate. Excluding it would make a region unshippable whenever its generator's filename carried the word, leaving *"rename the generator"* as the only remedy: the single-instance fix this lane rules against. Pinned with a case **plus a positive control proving the marker really carries the word**.

## The changeset red — mine to fix, and fixed

`Check Changeset` went red at 18:31:17Z for a missing changeset with no `skip-changeset` label. I applied the label **additively** (POST, ⛔ not a whole-set PUT, so a concurrent dev write could not be clobbered) after verifying nothing publishes: the diff is `scripts/check-role-word.mjs` only, `scripts/` matches **none** of the workspace globs, root is `private: true`. A fresh `Check Changeset` ran at 18:34:19Z and concluded **skipped**.

⚠️ Recorded because the record should say who did what: the **PM** applied that label, ⛔ not the dev, and the dev correctly did not write one after being told.

## Also worth recording

- The baseline ledger is **identical before and after** (43 files / 129 occurrences) — the three live regions carry no occurrence today, so ⛔ no baseline entry moves.
- Full `pnpm lint` repo-wide, exit 0. ⛔ No narrowing claimed, so none is owed.
- 15 gates derived, 15 run, `comm -23 derived ran` **empty**; `check:ratchet-remedy-authority` run explicitly per #13813 (green); `check-test-completeness` exit 3 = NOT MEASURED by its own text, ⛔ not a red.
- ⭐ A fourth ablation was **aborted by its own harness** when its anchor matched 2 sites, and was reported rather than silently re-run. An ablation whose mutation is ambiguous proves nothing, and catching that is the same discipline as the rest of this report.

## Governed-surface check

Diff is `scripts/check-role-word.mjs` only. ⛔ No hit on `docs/adr/**` · `.claude/**` · `skills/**` · `AGENTS.md` · `CLAUDE.md`. ⚠️ Note `skills/**` is inside the gate's *scan scope* but no file under it is modified ⇒ this seat may arm it.

## Arming

`Lint & Repo Gates` is still running, ⛔ zero real failures. Arming follows once it settles green.
